text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Compromise signals over coal subsidies seen from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition
- Auto tax will increase for many drivers in summer
- Number of business failures increases for the fifth time
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel renounces tax hike
- Kohl announces new construction business programme with investments of 25 billion marks
- Hoechst subsidiary's decision not to go public drags down chemical company stock on German market
- President of industry and trade council criticises unequal chances in telecommunications market
HANDELSBLATT
- Dax falls below 3400 points
- Bonn cranking up business with 25 billion mark investments
- More business is taking place over the Internet - Economics Minister Rexrodt
- Hoechst suffers drop on stock market
- Bonn wants to create more apprenticeships
- Waigel introduction of EMU should not affect the independence of the European Central Bank
- Kohl's coalition signals compromise with miners union
- Krupp stays with five mark dividend
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Kohl announces 25 billion mark investment in economic growth
- German Rail fails to reach investment quotas
- Number of business failings hits record
- Fifty percent of wine consumed in Germany comes from Germany
- Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits continues road show in Frankfurt, tries to drum up investment
DIE WELT
- Kohl announces billions in investment for German economy
- First move toward compromise in coal subsidies fight
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel warns of delay in the EMU
- Cebit computer fair opens in Hannover
- Rexrodt says computers bring efficiency in management and service at Cebit
- Health insurers and doctors criticise planned increase in patient co-payments for health care
- Leaders of IG Metall and Gesamtmetall industrial unions meet in Frankfurt, discuss part-time work and industry-wide pay contracts
- Kohl calls on Social Democrats to return to bargaining table on tax policy
- Drivers face increased 'pollution tax' -- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
